encounters.title: The Field Hospital
encounters.description: The war zone is a graveyard of ships. Amid the wreckage, a single station pulses with light — a makeshift hospital. Inside, a cat in a bloodstained apron works tirelessly, treating the wounded regardless of faction markings.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Sensors show a makeshift hospital station in the middle of this wreckage. Someone's running a field surgery in an active war zone.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: I'm reading multiple wounded — Lions, Corsairs, even Fairy folk. Whoever's in charge is treating everyone.

choices.text: Dock and offer your crew's help with the wounded.

outcome.description: Blood Paw barely looks up when you arrive. The wounded come first. Always.

choices.text: Watch from a distance before approaching.

outcome.description: You watch Blood Paw move between patients — treating them all the same, regardless of faction.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: We're docking now. My crew can help with the wounded — we have medical supplies aboard.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Supplies in the back. Sterile bandages, second shelf. Start with the critical cases — there's a Corsair with shrapnel in her lung and a Lion soldier who's lost too much blood.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: You're not going to ask who we are?

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: I don't care who you are. I care whether you can follow instructions and keep your hands clean. Can you do that?

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Good. And it's Doctor, not ma'am. Blood Paw. Former chief physician of the Lion court. Now — stop talking and start helping.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Former Lion court physician? What happened?

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: The court decided that healing should be political. I disagreed. Loudly. Now I treat everyone, and the court can sort out its own wounded.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Less talking. That Corsair's lung won't fix itself.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Let's hold position and watch. I want to understand what's happening in there before we commit.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: She's treating a Lion soldier. Now a Corsair pirate. A Fairy merchant. She doesn't even check their markings.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: You've been sitting out there for twelve minutes. I noticed you on sensors eight minutes ago.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: I — apologies. I was observing.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Observing. While people bleed. Fascinating approach.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: That's fair. I'm Captain Aristotle, Felid Corsair. We have medical supplies aboard.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Then stop observing and start unloading them. I'm Blood Paw. Former Lion court physician. Are you here to help, or to recruit? Because right now, I need the former.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Right now, we're here to help.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Then dock at airlock three. Wash your hands. And move quickly — I have patients who can't afford your caution.

encounters.title: Evacuation
encounters.description: Sensors flash: an incoming bombardment. The hospital station's shields won't hold. Every patient aboard will die unless someone acts now.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Sensors just lit up. Incoming bombardment — multiple warheads, ninety seconds out. The station's shields won't hold.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: How many can your ship carry?

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: If we clear the cargo bay... maybe all of them. It'll be tight.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Then clear the cargo bay. I'm not leaving a single patient behind. Not one.

choices.text: Open the cargo bay — we'll take everyone. Every last one.

outcome.description: It's a desperate rush. Your crew works alongside Blood Paw, carrying stretchers through buckling corridors.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Critical patients first. The Lion soldier on the spine board — careful with his neck. The Corsair with the chest drain goes next.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Sixty seconds. My crew is moving as fast as they can.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Faster. The ambulatory patients can walk — get them moving. You, with the Fairy merchant — support her left side, she has broken ribs.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Thirty seconds. The station's outer hull is buckling. Blood Paw, we need to go now.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: One more. There's a Goblin child in the back ward. I am not leaving without him.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: I'll get the child. You get to the ship.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Don't tell me where to go on my own station, Captain. I know these corridors. Move.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: The station is breaking apart — sealing the airlock now. Everyone's aboard. Everyone.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Count them. I need an exact count.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Thirty-seven patients. All accounted for.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Thirty-seven. Good. Now get us clear of the blast radius, and find me somewhere clean to set up triage. We're not out of the woods yet.

encounters.title: Blood Paw Joins the Crew
encounters.description: The evacuees are safe at a neutral station. Blood Paw finds you on the bridge, wiping her paws clean. The exhaustion in her eyes can't hide the steel underneath.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: All thirty-seven patients are stable. The neutral station has accepted them for ongoing care. My work here is done.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: You lost your hospital.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: I lost a building. The patients survived. That's the only metric that matters.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: What will you do now? Set up another field hospital?

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: I've been thinking about that. I left the Lion court because they forgot what healing means. They wanted me to prioritise — treat officers first, leave enemy wounded to die.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: And you couldn't do that.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: A wound doesn't care about politics. A broken bone doesn't check faction markings. I swore an oath to heal, and I meant it.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Yesterday, you opened your cargo bay for thirty-seven strangers. You didn't ask what faction they belonged to. You didn't calculate the cost.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: It was the right thing to do.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Yes. It was. And that's rare enough to be worth something.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Your crew will get hurt out there, Captain. Space combat, boarding actions, crystal mining accidents. You need a surgeon who won't let them die.

choices.text: The medbay is yours, Blood Paw. Keep my crew alive.

outcome.description: Blood Paw sets up the medbay with military precision — supplies sorted, instruments sterilised, emergency protocols posted.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Ship's Surgeon Blood Paw, reporting. First order of business — I need a full medical inventory and health assessments for every crew member. No exceptions.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Every crew member? Even the captain?

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Especially the captain. I've seen the way you eat. Cafeteria rations and engine-room coffee are not a nutritional strategy.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: I was hoping the ship's surgeon would be less... direct.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: Then you hired the wrong surgeon. I don't sugarcoat diagnoses, and I don't tolerate crew members who skip their checkups.

dialogue_steps.speaker: blood_paw
dialogue_steps.text: No one dies on my ship, Captain. That's not a promise — it's a policy.
